name: Brachydactyly Type E

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Brachydactyly Type E

criteria.description: Shortening of the metacarpals and metatarsals evident on radiographs
Shortened distal and/or middle phalanges of fingers and toes
Normal cognitive development without intellectual disability
Lack of other systemic malformations or syndromic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of shortening of metacarpals and/or metatarsals with characteristic phalangeal shortening on clinical and radiographic examination
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic imaging; genetic testing may identify mutations in PTHLH or related genes in some cases.

searchTerms: type E short fingers and toes
specific short digit pattern type E

occasional.symptomName: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the distal phalanx of the hallux
searchTerms: missing or small big toe tip bone
absent or small hallux tip bone
unequal size or strength of arms
one arm smaller or weaker than the other

imaging: Radiographs showing shortening of metacarpals and metatarsals
Radiographic evidence of shortened distal and middle phalanges
Possible delayed bone age on hand/wrist X-rays
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic brachydactyly hand and foot morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant shortening of distal phalanges of the thumbs
Isolated involvement of thumbs without metacarpal shortening
Brachydactyly type E features with endocrine abnormalities
Presence of hypocalcemia and elevated parathyroid hormone levels

redFlags: Progressive limb deformities beyond typical brachydactyly pattern
Presence of intellectual disability or developmental delay
Signs of systemic involvement suggesting syndromic diagnosis
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
